title: Minions & Monsters Didn't Smash Box Office Records — But It's Still a Winner!
summary: Have you ever seen a Minion? Those little yellow guys have been making us laugh for 15 years, and their newest movie, 'Minions & Monsters,' just hit theaters. But here's a surprise: it didn't break any records on its first weekend in the U.S. It earned $36.4 million, which is less than other Minions movies. But don't worry — the Minions are still superstars! The movie actually made $98.4 million in other countries already. That's because people all over the world love these silly characters. Plus, the movie got amazing reviews — it has a 91% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, which is the best score any Illumination film has ever gotten. So what's the story about? It's a 'totally true' (wink wink) tale of how the Minions became movie stars in the 1920s. They accidentally unleash real monsters while trying to make a monster movie, and then they have to save the world. Classic Minion chaos! The movie cost $85 million to make, which is less than many other animated films. So even if it doesn't earn a billion dollars like some earlier ones, it's still going to make a nice profit. And let's not forget all the Minion toys, backpacks, and banana-flavored snacks that will sell like crazy. So yes, the Minions might not be as huge as they once were, but they're still a big deal. As one expert said, 'Just because something isn't as big as it once was doesn't mean it's a failure.' So grab your goggles and head to the theater — the Minions are waiting!
why_it_matters: Even when a movie isn't as popular as earlier ones, it can still be a success — just like when a game you love still makes money even if fewer kids buy it.

background_read: Minions first appeared in the 2010 movie 'Despicable Me' and quickly became some of the most popular animated characters in the world.
Illumination is the movie studio behind the Minions and other hits like 'The Secret Life of Pets.'
Rotten Tomatoes is a site where critics rate movies; a high score means almost everyone who saw it liked it.
Article_Structure: WHO: The Minions and their new movie 'Minions & Monsters.'
WHAT: The movie earned $36.4 million in the U.S. but made $98.4 million from other countries and earned a 91% Rotten Tomatoes score.
WHERE: In theaters across the United States and in many other countries.
WHY: The Minions are loved around the world and the film's good reviews helped it still be profitable even if it didn't break U.S. records.

perspectives.description: The movie received the best reviews ever for an Illumination film, showing that quality matters to audiences.
Some people think the Minions are not as special as they once were, and lower U.S. ticket sales might mean fans are losing interest.
From a business view, the low production cost and strong earnings from other countries mean the movie will still make a nice profit.
